newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico approved GMexico-led bid for railways.
newsitem.headline: Mexico approved GMexico-led bid for railways.

text.p: Mexico approved on Thursday a bid by a consortium led by mining firm Grupo Mexico SA for 100 percent of the country's Pacific-North railway and the Topolobampo-Ojinaga railway.

The consortium, called Grupo Ferroviaria Mexicana (GFM), is composed of Grupo Mexico, with a 74 percent stake, Mexican builder Empresas ICA and U.S. Union Pacific, which each have a 13 percent stake in the bid.

"The bid today by Grupo Ferroviario Mexicano SA...complies in a broad and satisfactory manner with all the requisites for the (privatisation)..." the state-owned Mexican National Railway said in a statement.
GFM offered to pay 4.197 billion pesos, or $527.39 million, for both rail lines. The group also pledged earlier in the day to invest some 5 billion pesos over the next 10 years on the railways.
The group was initially bidding for just 80 percent of the Pacific-North line, but exercised an option to buy out full control and the nearby Topolobampo-Ojinaga line.
The National Railway said the sale, the second major privatisation of the formerly state-owned rail system, would help modernise the country's rail system.

It said the sale of the Pacific-North line, Mexico's largest with 3,875 miles of track, and the Topolobampo line would mean Mexico has privatised 80 percent of its rail system in terms of cargo tonnage.
